challengesToOtherFindings: The Industry Analyst's top insight correctly identifies the BEAD scale gap but stops short of the most actionable AE implication: Fybercom has zero in-house OSP design staff under the CTO. They are not a company trying to go faster with existing tools — they are a company that may not have a design workflow at all for a 12,000-location federal build. The risk is not slow design; it is no design. That reframes the conversation from 'efficiency tool' to 'deployment enabler.'

The AE's 'not a good fit' call was correct for the company that existed before October 2025. It is wrong for the company post-Novacap + BEAD award. The characterization ('short runs, not a lot of CAD') describes their history. It does not describe the obligation they accepted. This objection should be anticipated and addressed early — do not let the AE's prior framing kill the account before the conversation starts.

The Industry Analyst does not flag the Finance-background CTO signal. This materially changes the messaging approach: skip technical CAD workflow details, lead with permit-kickback financial exposure. Each permit kickback is 3-6 weeks of delayed federal milestone and potential compliance risk under the BEAD subgrant agreement. A Finance-trained CTO understands that risk calculus immediately.

The Industry Analyst frames CTO + OSP Director as a general 'vendor evaluation' pair. The sharper read: Smith is the problem owner who can describe the pain precisely; Calkins is the budget/tool decision authority who needs a business case. Email to Calkins should be short and ROI-framed; meeting agenda should include Smith for the workflow specifics. Two different conversations, not one.
topInsight: Fybercom has zero in-house OSP design or GIS/CAD staff under a Finance-trained CTO who now owns a $83M federal deployment obligation with a 4-year clock and a PE board watching velocity. The 'short runs, no CAD' AE concern is history — the obligation is now. The buying case is not 'make your design faster,' it is 'you are about to discover you have a design capacity gap when permits start coming back, and Inorsa can prevent the federal timeline from compressing.' Vince Calkins will buy on avoided cost and PE-board optics. Steve Smith is the workflow validator who needs to be in the room. Lead with permit-kickback exposure and federal milestone risk, not drawing generation speed.
